findings.rationale: Correct: a 1 MiB String read truncates and drops non-UTF-8 input, breaking R4. Folded into §3.1 together with 1b09e498: read raw bytes to EOF with no cap, parse JSON separately, forward the identical buffer; only an OS read error falls back to empty stdin.

Correct: the payload path keyed only by session_id+event can be overwritten by a later accepted call while the earlier worker still reads it, and the earlier worker would delete it. Folded into §3.3: each accepted call gets its own payload file created with O_EXCL under a unique name (session, event, pid, nanos), fully written before the worker starts; the worker reads and deletes only its own file; the session lock is separate.

Correct: session-digest is a codeforge wrapper that spawns node, so killing the wrapper does not prove the work stopped. Folded into §3.3: every step runs in its own process group and timeouts signal the whole group (TERM, grace, KILL); P2 test uses a fake chain that leaves a long-running grandchild.

Correct: hook::run's contract (Err -> exit 1, Ok(code) -> child exit code) contradicts R1. Folded into §3.1: the `on` branch is dispatched before hook::run's lookup, always ends the process with exit 0, swallows every error and child exit code (logged only), parses its own flags (--help, --detached, unknown) without clap; P1 binary tests cover unwritable data dir, non-JSON stdin, child exit 2, unknown event and unknown flag, all asserting exit 0.

Correct: exec_script inherits stdout, so a synchronous emit-session would leak bytes into session-end stdout, and the merge wording did not require re-serialising one object. Folded into §3.2/§3.3: no child ever inherits the parent stdout; session-start contexts are captured, emit-session goes to the log; session-start writes exactly one serde_json object with hookEventName SessionStart built from parsed strings, or nothing.
Same defect as 8d3e94b8 from the other seat; resolved the same way in §3.1 (raw bytes, no cap, empty only on OS read error, session_id parse never alters forwarded bytes).

Correct: the 60s stamp is shorter than the chain, so non-overlap must come from the lock alone. Folded into §3.3/§3.4: the detached worker takes the session lock before session-digest and holds it until ship is reaped; stale threshold (15 min) exceeds the sum of hard step deadlines plus grace; the stamp is documented as duplicate suppression only; P2 adds an overlapping-call test.

Correct: kill + unbounded wait and an un-budgeted stdin read can exceed the bridge timeout when a child ignores SIGTERM. Folded into §3.1–3.3: one wall-clock budget from process start (session-start 12s incl. reaping, session-end/pre-compact synchronous part 3s); stdin is read on a thread bounded by that budget; at the deadline TERM the child's group, 300 ms grace, KILL, bounded wait, then exit 0 regardless; lock waits happen only in the detached worker; P2 test uses a SIGTERM-ignoring fake child.
